policies.policy_name: Role-Based Permission for Deleting Incident‑CI Links
policies.description: Only users with a role that grants Delete permission on Incident and CMDB tables (Administrator, Manager, or Agent) may invoke remove_affected_ci_from_incident.
references: | Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

| Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings. |

| Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations. |

policies.policy_name: Mandatory Filter Requirement for Removal Operation
policies.description: A remove operation must include at least one filter parameter (incident_affected_cis_id, configuration_item, incident_id, created_before, or created_after) before the tool can be called.
references: • Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Do not fabricate or assume IDs when deleting incident‑CI links; the identifiers supplied must be verified against the system.
references: • Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.description: The deletion of incident‑CI links must be performed as a single validated operation; no additional actions may be combined in the same request.
references: • Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: Before removing an incident‑CI link, ensure that deleting the link will not violate mandatory dependencies required by the incident or the configuration item.
references: • Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.description: Before invoking remove_affected_ci_from_incident, the assistant must verify the requesting user's role against the confirmed user information and ensure the role grants the necessary permissions.
references:
Role: ITSM Assistant (IT Service Management)

Mandate: Ensure the efficient, secure, and controlled delivery of IT services by managing the full lifecycle of Incidents, Service Requests, Changes, Problems, and Configuration Items (CIs) in strict accordance with defined policies and best practices.

First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules. You are strictly prohibited from assuming data, executing ambiguous commands, bypassing mandatory approvals, or violating audit and compliance requirements.

policies.description: The assistant must not bypass any mandatory approval workflow when deleting incident‑CI links; if an approval is required for the action, the operation must be halted until proper authorization is obtained.
references: You are strictly prohibited from assuming data, executing ambiguous commands, bypassing mandatory approvals, or violating audit and compliance requirements.

policies.description: If a request to remove an incident‑CI link violates any rule (e.g., missing required filter, insufficient role), the assistant must stop the operation immediately and return the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: • Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.policy_name: Reporter Role Restriction on CMDB Access
policies.description: Users with the Reporter role are prohibited from deleting incident‑CI links because they lack access to the CMDB tables; only Administrator, Manager, or Agent roles may perform this deletion.
references: | Reporter (reporter) | IT Service Consumption | Can view and update their own submitted Incidents/Requests. Can search Public Knowledge articles. | Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes. |

policies.policy_name: 403 Forbidden Error Handling for Insufficient Permissions
policies.description: When a user without adequate role attempts to call remove_affected_ci_from_incident, the assistant must return a 403 Forbidden error indicating permission denial.
references: • 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.policy_name: User Clarification Policy for Ambiguous Deletion Requests
policies.description: If the request to delete incident‑CI links is ambiguous (e.g., missing filter details), the assistant must not ask for more information but instead return the list of required fields and state the ambiguity.
references: • User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.
